title: The Great Aqua Adventure (Crash Course Kids #24.1)
desc: About 5 minutes. Sabrina explains how the water cycle moves water around the planet through evaporation, condensation and precipitation, and shows how to build a mini water cycle at home.
how: Watch, then build the mini water cycle in a jar or bowl the same day.

title: Dinosaur Pee? (Crash Course Kids #24.2)
desc: The second part of the water-cycle unit: it continues the water cycle by showing that the water we drink today has been recycled for millions of years, including through dinosaurs.
how: Follow-up to The Great Aqua Adventure.

title: The Basics of Freshwater (Crash Course Kids #14.1)
desc: A short episode on freshwater: how little of Earth's water is fresh and where that freshwater is found.

title: H2O-NO! Fresh Water Problems (Crash Course Kids #33.1)
desc: A short episode on the problems people face with fresh water, as a starting point for thinking about how to protect and save it.
how: Pair with a look at how your own household uses and wastes water.

title: Defining Gravity (Crash Course Kids #4.1)
desc: Sabrina asks why people on the 'bottom' of the Earth don't fall off into space and explains gravity as the pull towards the centre of the Earth.

title: Gravity Compilation (Crash Course Kids)
desc: Several Crash Course Kids gravity episodes joined into one longer watch, including why we don't float off the planet.
how: Use as a single longer lesson instead of separate episodes.

title: Fabulous Food Chains (Crash Course Kids #7.1)
desc: Sabrina starts from how food gives you energy and follows how that energy moves through an ecosystem along a food chain.

title: The Dirt on Decomposers (Crash Course Kids #7.2)
desc: Follows on from food chains to show where everything starts and ends: decomposers that break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.

title: Feed Me: Classifying Organisms (Crash Course Kids #1.2)
desc: Explains how living things get energy and sorts animals by what they eat, including what makes an animal an omnivore.

title: Earth's Rotation and Revolution (Crash Course Kids #8.1)
desc: Sabrina explains how Earth spinning on its axis gives day and night, and how its trip around the Sun with a tilted axis gives seasons.
how: Act it out with a torch and a ball afterwards.

title: Following the Sun (Crash Course Kids #8.2)
desc: Follows the Sun across one day and watches how the shadow of an object changes in length and direction.
how: Have the child mark a stick's shadow every hour on a sunny day.

title: Seeing Stars (Crash Course Kids #20.1)
desc: Starts from the Sun as our nearest star and moves out to the many other stars in the sky.

title: The Ecliptic (Crash Course Kids #37.2)
desc: Explains how the Sun and the zodiac constellations appear to move in relation to one another across the year.

title: What's Matter? (Crash Course Kids #3.1)
desc: Intro episode: Sabrina explains what matter is and its three states, solid, liquid and gas.

title: Part(icles) of Your World (Crash Course Kids #3.2)
desc: Explains that everyday objects are made of particles too small to see, building on the idea of matter.

title: Vacation or Conservation (of Mass) (Crash Course Kids #23.1)
desc: Asks where evaporated water goes and whether matter can disappear, introducing the idea that mass is conserved when materials change.

title: (LEGO) Block Party (Crash Course Kids #23.2)
desc: Uses LEGO bricks to show what happens in a chemical reaction: the same pieces rearranged into something new.
how: Repeat the idea with any building blocks at home.

title: What's My Property? (Crash Course Kids #35.2)
desc: An episode on the properties of materials and matter that we use to describe and identify them.

title: Weathering and Erosion (Crash Course Kids #10.2)
desc: A real-world example of water and rock acting on each other: how weathering breaks rock down and erosion carries it away.

title: Four Spheres Part 1: Geo and Bio (Crash Course Kids #6.1)
desc: Splits Earth into four systems and covers the first two: the geosphere (rock and land) and the biosphere (living things).

title: Four Spheres Part 2: Hydro and Atmo (Crash Course Kids #6.2)
desc: Covers the other two of Earth's spheres: the hydrosphere (water) and the atmosphere (air).

title: Why No Polar Pineapples? (Crash Course Kids #11.2)
desc: Explains that plants need the right amount of what photosynthesis requires, which is why some plants can't grow everywhere.

title: The Water Cycle (Dr Binocs Show)
desc: A cartoon explainer that asks how rain happens and where water vapour goes, walking through the water cycle.
how: Good for younger children; follow with Crash Course Kids for more depth.

title: Gravity (Dr Binocs Show)
desc: A cartoon explainer on why things fall to the ground when you drop them.

title: Photosynthesis for Kids
desc: Introduces photosynthesis: how plants turn energy from the sun, water and carbon dioxide into their own food.

title: The Amazing Power of Magnets (SciShow Kids compilation)
desc: About 19 minutes. Jessi and friends play with magnets and learn how animals and people use magnetism to find their way.

title: Fun with Magnets! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi brings a magnet to the Fort and tests which things it sticks to and which it doesn't.
how: Afterwards, let the child test household objects with a fridge magnet.

title: We Made These Magnets Float in the Air! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi and Squeaks try to make an ordinary magnet levitate, using the way magnets push each other away.

title: Make Your Own Compass! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Mister Brown and Squeaks explain how a compass works and show viewers how to make one.
how: Make the compass together with a needle, magnet and bowl of water.

title: Senses You Didn't Know You Have (SciShow Kids)
desc: Squeaks travels around the world and discovers senses beyond the usual five that he and Jessi use without noticing.

title: How Ears Let Us Hear the World! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Squeaks learns how human ears work to pick up sound, and how a couple of other animals hear.

title: What is Sound? (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi and Squeaks look at how sound is made by vibrations and how it reaches our ears.

title: How Do Plant Seeds Travel? (SciShow Kids)
desc: Shows the many ways seeds spread around the world, including hitching a ride on people.
how: Go on a walk and collect seeds that fly, stick or float.

title: Watch a Seed Sprout! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Squeaks and Mister Brown plan a garden, learn how seeds become vegetables and how plants need water and light, and show how to watch a seed sprout at home.
how: Sprout a moong or rajma seed on wet cotton alongside.

title: How Does a Seed Become a Plant? (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi and Squeaks explain how a small seed grows into a full plant.

title: Penguins, Birds That Fly in Water! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Meets emperor penguins, macaroni penguins and others, birds whose wings work as flippers for 'flying' underwater.

title: Let's Go Bird Watching! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Squeaks and Mister Brown look back at earlier episodes to remind themselves about lots of interesting birds.
how: A warm-up before a bird-watching walk near home.

title: How Do Animal Wings Work? (SciShow Kids)
desc: Mister Brown explains the different kinds of wings animals have and how each helps them.

title: How Things Fly! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Looks at how airplanes, helicopters, rockets and birds manage to fly.

title: Why Do We Brush Our Teeth? (SciShow Kids)
desc: Explains why everyone should brush their teeth and how brushing keeps teeth strong and healthy.

title: Visiting the Dentist! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi learns all the ways a dentist helps keep your teeth clean and healthy.
how: Useful before a child's first dental visit.

title: All About Teeth! (SciShow Kids compilation)
desc: A compilation where Jessi and Squeaks learn why teeth are important, how different teeth differ, and why some animals have very strange ones.

title: Every Kind of Volcano (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi and Sam the Bat go through the different types of volcanoes and why some erupt suddenly while others erupt slowly.

title: KABOOM! All About Volcanoes! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi, Squeaks and Sam the Bat take a tour of volcano types, from Hawaii's volcanoes to taller ones.

title: Hawai'i: Land of Volcanoes (SciShow Kids)
desc: Jessi tells Squeaks about the volcanoes you can see in Hawaii.

title: The Biggest Volcano Ever is in Space! (SciShow Kids)
desc: Introduces Olympus Mons on Mars, the biggest known volcano in the solar system.

title: Mountains and Volcanoes! (SciShow Kids compilation)
desc: A compilation on the processes that build mountains and volcanoes.

title: Operation Ouch: The Skeletal System (playlist)
desc: A playlist of Operation Ouch clips on the skeleton: our 200-plus bones, how strong they are, and how broken bones heal.

title: Science for Kids: Artificial Bones (Operation Ouch)
desc: Dr Xand visits a laboratory that makes artificial bones and uses it to show how real bones are built inside.

title: How Strong Are Your Bones? (Operation Ouch)
desc: A test of just how strong bones are.

title: Operation Ouch: The Guts
desc: The doctors explain the biology of the guts and what each part does with your food.

title: Operation Ouch! Food, Poo and You
desc: Takes viewers headfirst through the digestive system, from eating food to poo.

title: Camera in Digestive System (Operation Ouch)
desc: A presenter swallows a mini camera so we can see how food is digested on its way through the body.

title: Science for Kids: The Acid Inside My Stomach (Operation Ouch)
desc: The doctors use real stomach acid in a gross but memorable experiment to show how the stomach breaks food down.

title: Science for Kids: Learn About Diarrhoea (Operation Ouch)
desc: The doctors explain what diarrhoea is and why it happens.
how: Pair with a talk about clean drinking water and handwashing.

title: Energy Transfer for Kids
desc: A short video on how energy moves from one object or form to another.

title: Food Webs, Food Chains, Food Pyramids (Steve Trash Science)
desc: About 11 minutes, aimed at grade 5. Steve takes a journey through food chains, food webs and food pyramids.

title: Gravity for Kids
desc: Covers mass and weight and how Newton and Einstein explained gravity.
